counting_method: Each review is tested against every theme and counted once in each theme it touches (multi-label). Theme counts therefore add up to more than the number of reviews; 1820 reviews (72.0%) touch at least one theme, 587 reviews touch two or more, and 707 reviews (28.0%) touch none (mostly very short, generic comments such as 'good' or 'bad', and neutral Reddit questions). Percentages use the 2,527-review dataset as denominator.
emergence: Themes were derived bottom-up: phrase-frequency scans of positive, negative, mixed and Reddit reviews, then reading random hits for every candidate issue code and re-coding until the unmatched negative reviews were mostly generic. 23 issue codes were grouped into five themes.

themes.name: Service quality, professional conduct and trust (good and bad)
themes.definition: What the professional actually delivers: skilled, punctual and courteous work on the positive side; poor or incomplete work, damage or theft, rude or unsafe conduct and dishonesty on the negative side.

evidence_score.formula: 0.40*reach(n/largest theme) + 0.30*share Negative/Mixed + 0.15*share of the 4 sources where the theme is in >=5% of reviews + 0.15*min(1, 2*share of theme reviews that are Non-Return by Stated or Signalled evidence)

sides.note: T4 is two-sided: it holds most of the positive evidence (what customers value) and the quality/conduct/trust failures.

themes.interpretation: Customers' view of the individual professional decides most of the Return evidence: 441 of the 548 Return reviews that state or signal it sit in this theme, mostly praising skill, politeness and punctuality, and naming specific professionals they would book again. The same theme holds 441 failure reviews (poor work, damage or theft, conduct, trust), so quality variance between professionals is the central tension.

themes.name: Support access, refunds and problem resolution (including warranty and Native after-sales)
themes.definition: Customers cannot reach a human, wait for refunds, see complaints closed without resolution, or are refused warranty and rework, including Native purifier installation and after-sales.

evidence_score.formula: 0.40*reach(n/largest theme) + 0.30*share Negative/Mixed + 0.15*share of the 4 sources where the theme is in >=5% of reviews + 0.15*min(1, 2*share of theme reviews that are Non-Return by Stated or Signalled evidence)

themes.interpretation: The largest problem theme. The initial failure is often not what ends the relationship: customers describe being unable to reach a person, waiting for refunds, having complaints closed, or being refused warranty. 231 of the 468 reviews also report a primary failure (late/no-show, poor work, damage, price), so recourse failures compound other problems. Native purifier after-sales is a distinct cluster (94 reviews).

themes.name: Unreliable fulfilment: cancellations, no-shows, delays and missing slots
themes.definition: Booked services that are cancelled, rescheduled, late, never attended, or cannot be booked because no professional or slot is available.

subthemes.name: Cancelled by the company or professional

evidence_score.formula: 0.40*reach(n/largest theme) + 0.30*share Negative/Mixed + 0.15*share of the 4 sources where the theme is in >=5% of reviews + 0.15*min(1, 2*share of theme reviews that are Non-Return by Stated or Signalled evidence)

themes.interpretation: Customers treat a booking as a commitment and arrange their day, leave or an occasion around the slot. 85.0% of these reviews are Negative. Cancellations (127), no-shows (82) and lateness (89) dominate; they are strongest on PissedConsumer (48.5% of its reviews) and ConsumerComplaints (23.0%) where customers escalate, but also appear in 9.4% of Google Play reviews.

themes.name: Price, fees and policy rigidity
themes.definition: Prices that feel high or keep rising, platform/visit/cancellation fees, minimum-order and plan rules, and extra charges or parts upselling by professionals.

subthemes.name: Platform, visit and cancellation fees; policy rigidity

evidence_score.formula: 0.40*reach(n/largest theme) + 0.30*share Negative/Mixed + 0.15*share of the 4 sources where the theme is in >=5% of reviews + 0.15*min(1, 2*share of theme reviews that are Non-Return by Stated or Signalled evidence)

themes.interpretation: Price is rarely the only complaint: customers object to prices changing between the quote and the bill, to fees stacked on a small job (visit, platform, cancellation), and to parts or extras suggested by the professional. Customers compare directly with local providers (see alternatives). 25.5% of the Non-Return reviews that say so outright or signal it (advise against, switching, distrust) raise price or fees.

themes.name: Coverage gaps, missing services and app friction
themes.definition: Services or areas Urban Company does not cover, services customers ask for that do not exist, and app, location or usability problems.

subthemes.name: Service not available in the area or city
App bugs, location or usability issues

evidence_score.formula: 0.40*reach(n/largest theme) + 0.30*share Negative/Mixed + 0.15*share of the 4 sources where the theme is in >=5% of reviews + 0.15*min(1, 2*share of theme reviews that are Non-Return by Stated or Signalled evidence)

themes.interpretation: A smaller but consistent theme of unmet needs: unavailable areas and cities, services customers ask for that do not exist, and app/location friction. It is mostly expressed as requests, so it is lower in volume but rich in product direction.

note: T4 ranks highest because it is the broadest and holds the positive evidence. Among problem-focused themes the order of evidence is T3, T2, T1 (T1 and T2 are nearly tied).
